Case_19001/figure1.jpg.source_caption: Ziehl-Neelsen stain of the 30°C broth culture after 14 days of incubation. Acid fast bacilli with cord formation are seen.

description.short_caption: Ziehl-Neelsen stain showing acid-fast bacilli with cord formation.
description.detailed_description: This image shows a Ziehl-Neelsen stain of a culture specimen. Numerous pink, slender, rod-shaped acid-fast bacilli are visible, arranged in a characteristic cord-like formation against a pale background. The staining highlights the mycolic acid-rich cell walls of the organisms, which retain the red dye despite decolorization. This pattern is typical of certain mycobacterial species.
visible_findings: pale background with no other structures visible

description.detailed_description: This image shows a Middlebrook 7H11 agar plate with rough, white colonies growing on its surface. The colonies are irregularly distributed and have a textured appearance. The plate is being held by a gloved hand, and the background appears to be a laboratory setting. The colonies are consistent with the growth of certain mycobacterial species.
